classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and the supplementary-angle relationship to two supplied triangle configurations.

content.prompt:
Two triangles are shown, with sides 6 cm and 4 cm. The angle opposite the 4 cm side is $36^\circ$.

Find, in each case, the angle opposite the 6 cm side, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Two triangles side by side with horizontal bases and 36° at their lower-right vertices. The left triangle has an obtuse lower-left angle; the right has an acute lower-left angle. Ordinary source strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle has a 4 cm side opposite 36° and a 6 cm side opposite the required lower-left angle. The two configurations correspond to supplementary solutions.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and 36° angles are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle opposite the 6 cm side.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{6}&=\frac{\sin36^\circ}{4}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{6\sin36^\circ}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The acute possibility is
$$\begin{align*}\theta_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6\sin36^\circ}{4}\right)\\\theta_1&\approx61.8454^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The obtuse possibility is
$$\begin{align*}\theta_2&=180^\circ-\theta_1\\\theta_2&\approx118.1546^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Both are valid because $36^\circ+118.1546^\circ<180^\circ$.

The left triangle has the obtuse angle, so its required angle is $118^\circ$. The right triangle has the acute angle, so its required angle is $62^\circ$, to the nearest degree.
